Their fluency was notable, as seen in "This man in the suit looks completely unbothered and confident like he owns the fountain." Also, their confidence shone through in "I would be too embarrassed to do this myself but I admire his attitude completely."

THE MAIN PROBLEM
The biggest issue was the lack of a clear position, as shown in "Maybe he made a bet with his colleagues and had to do this as a dare," which indicates uncertainty.

THE PATTERN
Across turns 1, 2, and 3, they used phrases like "I think" and "maybe," which can make them seem less confident to a listener, as seen in "I think he is celebrating a promotion or some major personal victory."

CONFIDENCE REPORT
Total hedging signals found: 2. Top signals: "I think" and "maybe." The worst moment was "Maybe he made a bet with his colleagues and had to do this as a dare," which signals uncertainty to a listener.

THREE THINGS TO FIX
POINT: Filler words disrupt fluency. REASON: It makes the listener focus on the filler instead of the message. EXAMPLE: "This man in the suit looks completely unbothered and confident like he owns the fountain" has a filler. TRY THIS INSTEAD: "This man in the suit looks confident like he owns the fountain."
POINT: Hedging signals undermine confidence. REASON: It makes the listener question the speaker's certainty. EXAMPLE: "I think he is celebrating a promotion or some major personal victory." TRY THIS INSTEAD: "He is likely celebrating a promotion or some major personal victory."
POINT: Sentence structure can be more varied. REASON: It keeps the listener engaged. EXAMPLE: "I would be too embarrassed to do this myself but I admire his attitude completely." TRY THIS INSTEAD: "His attitude is admirable, even if I wouldn't do it myself."

ONE EARNED ENCOURAGEMENT

SPOKEN SUMMARY
You spoke casually, but sometimes lacked clarity. Try reducing filler words for better fluency. You have potential, let's build on it.
